title: personal-okr-weekly-checkin-hunter-ellis-2026-03-29
content:
Weekly OKR / KPI check-in - Hunter Ellis
Week of 2026-03-29

Quick summary:
- Focus this sprint: reduce p99 tail latency for text-generation endpoint (chat-completion) and make progress on cost reduction via KV prefix caching + quantization pipeline.
- Feeling: making steady progress on profiling + kernel tuning, but blocked on extended stress windows and infra GPU time for large-scale load tests.

OKR (Q2 2026) - personal / eng-serving-runtime contribution:
O: Improve inference economics & reliability for the hosted chat endpoint
KR1: Reduce p99 latency from 420ms -> <= 300ms for 95% of traffic (target by 2026-06-30)
  - Current: 420ms p99 (baseline Jan 2026)
  - This week: 385ms p99 (after small scheduler tweaks + kernel patch) -> progress ~30%
KR2: Deploy KV prefix caching to 80% of steady-state traffic
  - Current: feature rollout at 54% traffic (canary -> regional rollout in progress) -> progress ~67%
KR3: Deliver 8-bit quantization pipeline + validation for 2 top models (text-gen-large, code-gen-medium)
  - Current: quant pipeline WIP, unit tests passing, integration training for model A in progress -> progress ~40%

Weekly metrics / numbers:
- p50: 42ms (stable)
- p95: 110ms (improved)
- p99: 385ms (down from 420ms)
- Avg cost per 1k tokens: $0.82 -> after batching/kv improvements estimate $0.70 (projected)
- KV cache hit rate (canary region): 63% (need 80% to meet KR)

Progress notes / what I did this week:
- Ran distributed profile (small-scale) comparing kernel versions v1.8.2 vs v1.9.0 -> identified tensor reorder overhead on long-context paths. Filed ENGINF-412 (see linked_artifacts)
- Landed micro-batching changes for non-blocking IO (PR #987) -> reduced p95 by ~10ms
- Worked with Maya to instrument more detailed KV cache telemetry (latency buckets + hit origin tagging)
- Started integration tests for 8-bit quant flow: baseline accuracy regression test harness + smoke tests running on TPU-sim nodes

Blockers / open questions:
- Need longer GPU time on gold cluster to run high-concurrency stress tests (requested via infra queue, currently waiting for allocation - Noah following up)
- Policy question: do we want to accept small (<=1%) output-quality regression during aggressive quantization in exchange for cost wins? Need product/rls guidance.
- Observability gap: rollout dashboard doesn't surface per-customer KV hit skew -> hard to prioritize customer-specific fixes. Follow-up with Console team.

Next week plan (concrete):
- Get at least one full 24h high-concurrency stress run on gold cluster -> measure p99 under sustained load (owner: Noah/infra)
- Ship KV cache rollout to EU region (canary success criteria: error rate < 0.1% and latency delta < +5ms)
- Finish integration harness for quantization and run validation across 5 evaluation prompts (owner: me + Samira)
- Pair with Maya on building per-route cache skew view in Console (scoping meeting Wed)

Notes to self / TODOs (short):
- Follow up ENGINF-412 with kernel engineers for proposed reorder patch (link PR once created)
- Add additional test cases for code-gen edge-case where kv prefix truncation caused hallucination (see ticket #CG-77)
- Prepare short exec slide (1 slide) showing cost vs latency tradeoff for Monday leadership sync

Meeting agenda items for 2026-03-30 sync:
1) Status on gold cluster allocation + acceptance criteria for stress run
2) Decide quantization policy tradeoff + how to present to product/legal
3) Console telemetry ask: per-tenant KV hit skew view (Maya to present mock)
4) Rollout cadence for KV cache to remaining regions

Random notes / rough thoughts (brainstorm):
- Could we try adaptive cache TTLs based on recent request similarity? Might bump hit rate for some bursty customers.
- Idea: fast-fail fallback to smaller model variant when tail latency spikes > threshold to keep success rate high (need SRE buy-in).

Links / references:
- Canary KV rollout metrics dashboard (internal): /dashboards/kv-rollout-canary (Console)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Jira: ENGINF-412
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=83429123

End.
